newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair Sept '96 cargo traffic up 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swissair Sept '96 cargo traffic up 8 pct.

text.p: Swissair said September 1996 cargo traffic rose by eight percent on the same month last year to 136.1 million freight tonne kilometres (FTK).
On all Swissair's long-haul routes, with the exception of Japan, cargo volumes grew in comparison with September 1995.
Increases were mainly due to regular full-freighter capacity on these routes, the airline added.
October 30 saw the inaugural flight of a twice-weekly full-freighter service between Geneva and Singapore.
The strongest growth in cargo traffic was recorded on Swissair's South America routes where volumes rose by 60 percent on 1995 levels to 5.9 million FTK.
At the end of September 1996, Swissair launched a weekly DC10-30F service between Basel and Sao Paulo.
As in previous months, European traffic suffered from the reduced cargo capacity of the Airbus fleet with volumes down nine percent on September 1995 at 4.9 million FTK, it said.
"The decline is slower than during the first months of 1996 and there are indications, however weak, that pan-European air cargo traffic might pick up again."
